jobs.prompt: Write docs/security-gate.md in plain, short sentences, from the code and the A1 spec in your context. Sections: what the gate is and where it runs (the merge queue, on every batch, after the batch's files are written and before it can stay merged; a block rolls the batch back and the queue bisects it like a failed check); the five checks (secret scan with the rules listed by name and that findings never contain the secret, only a 12 character fingerprint; package check: every new dependency must exist on the registry, be at least 30 days old, have real downloads (at least 100 last week) and not look like a popular name; known vulnerabilities from npm audit, pip-audit or osv-scanner, high and critical block, only when a manifest or lockfile changed in the batch; code scan with semgrep when installed: high and medium findings become fix tickets and never block; licence check: GPL and AGPL block unless allowed, LGPL and permissive licences pass, an unknown licence only warns); what a block does (the check name security-gate in checkFailed, securityBlocked in the queue state and summary, an inbox blocker with the id security-<run>-<jobs> and no secret text, one sanitized lesson line in .swarm/project/security-lessons.ndjson for the Phase 15 lessons loop); the policy: the optional security block in .project-swarm.json profile with every key and its default (enabled true, minAgeDays 30, minWeeklyDownloads 100, blockSeverities high and critical, allowCopyleft false, approvedLicenses, allowedSecretFingerprints) and that it can only be turned off there (never by a flag; it also runs with --no-checks); how to allow a known false positive (the marker swarm-secret-allow on the line, or the fingerprint in allowedSecretFingerprints); missing tools are skipped with a note (npm, pip-audit, osv-scanner, semgrep) and an unreachable registry fails closed for new dependencies; the known limits (it scans only files a batch writes, not history; the registry checks need network; a weekly download count is only a signal).

Return `edits` (exact old text found once, and its replacement) using the anchors given; change nothing else. In docs/merge-queue.md, directly before the heading line "## Crash safety" (use that heading as the anchor and keep it), add a section "## Security gate" with two short paragraphs: every batch also goes through the security gate (secret scan, new-package check, known vulnerabilities, code scan, licence check) after its files are written; a block fails the batch like a failed check (rolled back, bisected, recorded in checkFailed as security-gate, listed in securityBlocked with an inbox blocker and a sanitized lesson) and --no-checks does not skip it; and a link to [the security gate](security-gate.md) for the details and the profile security policy.

Edit CHANGELOG.md in place; change nothing else. Insert a new section directly after the line "# Changelog" (and a blank line) titled "## 1.79.0" with this bullet: "- Security gate on every merge-queue batch (A1): after a batch's files are written and before it can stay merged, `integrate --queue` runs a secret scan (built-in rules; a finding has only a fingerprint, never the secret), a new-dependency check (must exist on npm or PyPI, be at least 30 days old, have real downloads, not look like a popular name; fails closed when the registry is unreachable), known-vulnerability checks (npm audit, pip-audit, osv-scanner; high and critical block; only when a manifest or lockfile changed), a Semgrep code scan when installed (findings become fix tickets, never a block) and a licence check (GPL and AGPL block unless the owner allows). A block rolls the batch back and bisects it like a failed check (`security-gate` in `checkFailed`, `securityBlocked` in the summary), opens an inbox blocker with no secret text and writes a sanitized lesson to `.swarm/project/security-lessons.ndjson`. The policy is the optional `security` block of the project profile; it can only be disabled there, never by a flag, and it also runs with `--no-checks`. See [security gate](docs/security-gate.md)."
